security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples, OpenAPI placeholders, and route identifiers. One contextual risk remains: the OpenAPI template recommends npx validation commands, which can execute third-party packages if run automatically.

remediation.issue: OpenAPI validation guidance uses npx package execution.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before running validation commands, pin package versions, or recommend trusted local installations.

semantic_findings.title: External Package Execution Suggested
semantic_findings.description: The OpenAPI template suggests npx commands for swagger-cli and redocly validation. If an agent runs these without user approval or pinned versions, it may execute downloaded third-party packages.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited lines explicitly present npx validation commands. They use common developer tools, but npx can fetch and execute package code, so agent execution should require confirmation.

content.value_statement: API teams need consistent contracts before implementation. This skill guides REST, GraphQL, OpenAPI, errors, versioning, and security choices.
actual_capabilities: Design resource-based REST endpoints and method mappings.
Define status codes, success responses, and error responses.
Plan pagination, versioning, authentication, and rate limiting.
Draft GraphQL query, mutation, type, and input patterns.
Use an OpenAPI 3.0 template for API documentation.
Review API designs against a validation checklist.
limitations: It does not implement server code or database models.
It needs product requirements to choose accurate resources.
The OpenAPI template is generic and needs project details.
Validation commands require local tooling and user approval.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Product API
use_cases.description: Define resources, endpoints, request shapes, responses, and security rules before engineering starts.

use_cases.title: Review an API Contract
use_cases.description: Check endpoint naming, status codes, pagination, versioning, and error consistency before release.

use_cases.title: Document an Existing Service
use_cases.description: Turn known endpoints and schemas into a clear OpenAPI structure for clients and partners.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic REST API
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a REST API for [product area]. Include resources, endpoints, methods, status codes, and simple response descriptions.

prompt_templates.title: Add Errors and Pagination
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this API idea: [description]. Add pagination, validation errors, authentication needs, rate limits, and consistent response rules.

prompt_templates.title: Compare REST and GraphQL
prompt_templates.prompt: For [use case], compare REST and GraphQL designs. Recommend one approach and explain endpoint or schema tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an OpenAPI Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this API contract for naming, security, versioning, error handling, pagination, and documentation gaps. Return prioritized changes.

output_examples.input: Design endpoints for a customer support ticket service.
output: Defines ticket, comment, assignment, and attachment resources.
Maps list, create, update, close, and reopen operations to REST methods.
Includes pagination, authorization notes, and error response guidance.

output_examples.input: Review an API contract for a billing service.
output: Flags inconsistent invoice and payment naming.
Suggests clearer conflict and validation responses.
Adds versioning and rate limit documentation requirements.

output_examples.input: Plan a GraphQL API for user profiles.
output: Proposes core query and mutation responsibilities.
Defines profile, account, and preference types at a high level.
Notes authorization and pagination requirements for related data.

best_practices: Start with resources and relationships before choosing endpoint paths.
Use consistent response envelopes, status codes, and error details.
Document authentication, authorization, pagination, and versioning early.
anti_patterns: Do not design endpoints around verbs when resources are clearer.
Do not expose sensitive data in URLs or error messages.
Do not publish an API contract without validation and review.

faq.question: Does this skill generate implementation code?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on API design, contracts, documentation, and review guidance.

faq.question: Can it help with both REST and GraphQL?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes REST endpoint patterns and GraphQL schema design patterns.

faq.question: Does it include OpenAPI guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It links to an OpenAPI 3.0 template and recommends validation steps.

faq.question: Can it review an existing API?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the contract or endpoint list, then ask for gaps and improvements.

faq.question: Does it cover API security?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers HTTPS, authentication, authorization, validation, rate limits, and sensitive data handling.

faq.question: Should validation commands run automatically?
faq.answer: No. Commands that install or execute packages should run only after explicit user approval.
